background: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: finished distant background panorama for a 2D side-scrolling Gothic action game's forest level, SNES/GBA-quality detailed pixel art, intended to be reduced to 1024 by 480 pixels. Reference image is STYLE ONLY: match its deep navy shadows, fine restrained pixel texture, atmospheric Gothic architecture. Create a distinct haunted forest at night: broad gnarled ancient tree silhouettes, dense muted emerald and teal foliage, layered blue-green mist, a few distant ruined Gothic towers barely visible through trees. Wide landscape composition, distant scenery only, no foreground walkable ground or platforms, no characters, no UI, no writing. Trees and ruined towers should have large readable silhouettes rather than busy tiny details. The center and upper sky should be dark and calm so bright enemies remain readable. Palette predominantly midnight blue, forest teal and subdued green; faint silver-blue mist, no bright neon green. Flat side-view backdrop, no vanishing-point road. Horizontal edges have compatible dark tree density for repetition. Opaque image.
ember: Use case: style-transfer. Asset type: production transparent pixel-art enemy sprite source for Gothic SNES/GBA action game, three poses arranged left to right in three equally spaced columns. Reference image shows the exact native three silhouettes: retain those proportions and direction. Repaint as the same small golden ember demon, with an ochre horned head, blunt projecting snout, glowing ivory eye, compact curled body, little claws and fiery gold tail. First pose is the compact front-facing crouched/curled shape. Second is left-facing head with tucked body/tail beneath. Third uses EXACTLY the same head and upper torso as second, but unfurls its tail toward the lower right. Keep the upper half of poses two and three identical. Readable chunky pixel clusters, antique gold, chestnut shadows, warm ivory highlights, dark outline. No new limbs outside the reference silhouettes. Not a human, no weapons. Each pose isolated, no overlap, no labels or UI. Truly transparent background. This is finished source art for a 32x32,32x32,48x32 pixel registration: broad details, no painterly blur, no fine noisy texture.
flyer: Use case: style-transfer. Asset type: tiny enemy animation sprite source, two poses side by side in equal columns. Reference image is native sprite anatomy and silhouette: two small swept bat wings at top, a long slim pale pink body hanging vertically in center. Repaint as a tiny crimson cavern bat with two vivid red wings and pale pink membranes, a narrow ivory-pink central body, tiny dark face with red eyes. Left pose wings raised into a wide V, right pose wings bent down and spread to the sides. The central body must be identically placed and same size in both poses. Match native overall footprint 16x16 pixels (will be registered at32x32). Fine SNES/GBA-quality Gothic pixel art, crisp clusters and readable outline, restrained palette of crimson, burgundy shadow, rose, ivory. No huge ears, no feet extending past the original body, no separate background, no lettering, no other objects. Truly transparent background, fully isolated two sprites.
bark: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: seamless game texture for the face of a very wide ancient tree trunk in a 2D Gothic platformer, intended to reduce to a 96 by 32 pixel repeating tile. Generate ONLY flat, front-facing bark material filling the whole wide landscape image edge to edge. Long vertical ridges and vertical fissures run cleanly through the top and bottom edges; no diagonal stripes, no horizontal bands, no crosswise branches, no circular knots. Large readable vertical grooves with subdued warm brown and antique bronze highlights, deep dark-brown/navy crevices. Detailed SNES/GBA pixel art, crisp pixel clusters. Natural wood, not stone, not brick, not a log pile. Subtle edge lighting from upper left. Relatively even colors across the whole texture so repeated tiles join. No sky, no ground, no objects, no border, no text. Opaque. Aspect ratio3:1.
